base_record_snapshot.lesson: A fail-soft fallback COUNTER must be keyed per fallback-REASON FAMILY, not carried as a single scalar over 'did we fall back' — because a fail-soft surface's fallback reasons routinely span families with OPPOSITE operational meanings, and a reason-blind counter converts a healthy refusal into a false outage alarm (and vice versa). The harmony voice lane is the proof. Its 116-row voice history carries exactly two families: (a) INFRASTRUCTURE failure — llm_timeout_45s fired 8 consecutive tics 677-684 at ~45017ms, plus llm_error:* / empty_output — where the engine never obtained an answer, and consecutive runs are a genuine outage that must escalate loudly; and (b) ADMISSION-GATE refusal — validation_failed:multi_line (tic 670), validation_failed:imperative_vocabulary (tic 686) — where the transport SUCCEEDED, produced a line, and the validator correctly REFUSED it because an ambient non-citable voice must not be imperative. Family (b) is the gate WORKING; harmony-voice.py's own selftest fixture [6] asserts this arm as correct behavior. The filed fix bk-harmony-fallback-consecutive-counter (ratified /review 685, still UNBUILT) specifies 'track consecutive template_fallback runs ... escalate at threshold N>=2' — a scalar over voice_source==template_fallback, reason-blind by construction. Tic 686 is the live counterexample arriving one tic after filing and before building: t685 was healthy (llm, 73114ms) so the scalar resets to 0; t686 fell back on a HEALTHY VALIDATOR REFUSAL so the scalar reads 1; a second such refusal at 687 would trip the N>=2 escalation and report an infrastructure outage that is not occurring. The inverse error is equally real: a scalar that resets on any success can never surface that the admission-gate family has now fired twice 16 tics apart (670, 686), which is the signal that the PROMPT is drifting toward imperative phrasing — a real quality regression on its own, slower escalation curve. Therefore: key the counter on the reason family, give each family its own threshold and escalation semantics (infrastructure -> outage/loud escalation at small N; admission-gate -> prompt-drift/quality watch over a longer window, explicitly NOT an outage), and preserve the distinction in whatever signal or stderr channel the counter drives. Generalizes beyond harmony: any fail-soft lane whose fallback taxonomy mixes 'the dependency failed' with 'our own gate refused the output' needs the same split, because fail-soft removes the escalation channel and a reason-blind replacement channel restores volume without restoring meaning.
